**Q2. What experimental evidence led Rutherford to conclude that the central part (nucleus) of an atom is positively charged?** Some alpha particles (about 1 in 10,000) were deflected by as much as 90Â° or even larger angles. Since alpha particles are positively charged, they could only be repelled by a positively charged centre â€” proving the nucleus is positively charged.

**Q3. What experimental evidence led Rutherford to conclude that the atom consists mostly of hollow or empty space?** The vast majority of alpha particles (about 99%) passed straight through the gold foil completely undeflected, showing that most of the space inside the atom is empty.

**Q4.
